name: tutorial_lobbying_triage
document:
# Tutorial: Lobbying Disclosure Triage (synthetic sample)

## Purpose

Federal lobbying disclosures (Senate LDA "LD-2" filings) report which client hired which
registrant, how much was spent, and — in a free-text "specific lobbying issues" field —
what they lobbied on. That free-text field is where the substance is, and it is messy.
This five-step tutorial workflow narrows a quarter of filings to the ones with real money
behind them, reads the issue text of each, and flags the ones a reporter should look at
again.

The sample data is SYNTHETIC and BUNDLED with this tutorial — invented organizations and
invented issue text, shaped like a real Senate LDA export. It is not live LDA data, and no
row in it describes a real filing, a real client, or a real lobbying firm. Nothing is
fetched from the network.

## Input data

A single bundled CSV, `tutorial_lobbying_triage.csv`, one row per filing, with columns:

- `filing_id` — stable, unique identifier for the filing
- `client` — the organization that retained the lobbyists
- `registrant` — the lobbying firm that filed the disclosure
- `amount_usd` — reported lobbying spend for the period, in whole US dollars
- `filing_period` — the reporting period, e.g. "2024 Q1"
- `specific_issues` — the filer's free-text description of the specific issues lobbied

## Step 1 — Keep the filings above $50,000

Drop every filing reporting less than $50,000 of spend for the period; a filing reporting
exactly $50,000 is kept (the threshold is inclusive). Kept filings pass through unchanged.
A filing reporting no amount at all is not guessed either way — the step stops and says so.

## Step 2 — Classify each filing's issue text (LLM)

For each surviving filing, read the `specific_issues` free text and add three fields — one
filing in, one filing out (the filing is neither dropped nor duplicated):

- `policy_area` — the single best-fit policy area, one of: Health, Energy & Environment,
  Finance & Taxation, Technology, Defense, Transportation, Agriculture, Other.
- `targets_specific_bill` — true if the issue text names a specific piece of legislation
  (for example a bill number like "H.R. 3684" or "S. 1234", or a named Act), false otherwise.
- `primary_ask` — a single plain-language sentence summarizing what the client appears to want.

Filings are read twelve at a time in one model call. This step makes no judgment about spend.

## Step 3 — Flag the filings worth a second look

Add `needs_followup`, decided from Step 2's two judgments and nothing else: a filing needs
follow-up when it names no specific bill, or when it landed in the catch-all Other policy
area. Both cases mean the issue text alone did not pin down what was being lobbied for. A
filing whose classification is blank is not guessed — the step stops and says so.

## Step 4 — Publish the triage report

Produce a single HTML page listing every surviving filing with client, registrant, reported
spend, policy area, the primary ask and the issue text as filed. A flagged filing also shows
which of Step 3's two conditions flagged it — no specific bill named, the catch-all Other
area, or both — so the page carries the argument for a second look rather than a bare flag.
No score, no ranking and no recommendation — the report is a reading aid, not a verdict.

The page's markup and stylesheet are a committed template file, not text assembled inside the
step; the step fills its placeholders and writes the result.

## Out of scope

No external fetching, no human-review queue, and no joins — a single linear pass from the
bundled CSV to the published report.

connector.notes: The synthetic CSV bundled beside this fixture as app/seeds/data/tutorial_lobbying_triage.csv, mirroring the Senate LDA LD-2 export shape. No path is recorded here — the file is bound when a run starts. Nothing is fetched from the network.

stages.description: Keep filings reporting at least $50,000 of spend
compiler_notes: The threshold is inclusive on the low side: a filing reporting exactly $50,000 is kept.
amount_usd is declared non-null upstream, so a blank amount is already a schema violation; the predicate refuses rather than reading a blank as zero, which would drop the filing silently.

filter.summary: Keeps a filing when its reported spend is $50,000 or more, and drops it when it is less. A filing reporting no amount at all is not decided either way — the step stops and says which filing it was.

corner_cases.expected: the filing is kept — the threshold is inclusive

corner_cases.case: a filing reports no `amount_usd` at all
corner_cases.expected: the step fails, naming the filing, rather than dropping it

compiler_notes: Grain is strictly 1:1 — the document explicitly states no filing is dropped or duplicated in this step.
policy_area enum is closed; max_retries handles a hallucinated category value by letting the model retry on schema mismatch.

targets_specific_bill may produce false negatives when legislation is cited by colloquial name only (e.g. 'the farm bill') rather than a formal bill number or named Act — this limitation is not addressed in the source document.

batch_size 12 amortizes the instructions prefix across twelve filings per call, and each call is a process spawn, so the batch size sets how long a run takes; the filings in a batch share one context, which the document accepts for a per-filing classification this coarse.
client and filing_period are passed into the prompt as context only; they do not change the classification logic.

llm.prompt_instructions:
You are a policy analyst triaging federal lobbying disclosures.

Return a JSON object with exactly these three fields:

1. "policy_area": the single best-fit category from this fixed list — choose exactly one:
   Health | Energy & Environment | Finance & Taxation | Technology | Defense | Transportation | Agriculture | Other

2. "targets_specific_bill": true if the text names a specific piece of legislation (e.g. a bill number such as H.R. 3684 or S. 1234, or a named Act), false otherwise.

3. "primary_ask": a single plain-language sentence (no jargon) summarising what the client appears to want from government.

stages.description: Flag filings whose issue text did not pin down a bill
compiler_notes: Decided from targets_specific_bill and policy_area alone — no spend, no client, no re-reading of the issue text.
Both inputs are nullable because the classifier may leave them blank; a blank is refused rather than read as 'no bill', which would flag a filing the pipeline never actually judged.

adds.name: needs_followup
adds.description: True when the filing is worth a reporter's second look: the classifier tied it to no named bill, or it landed in the catch-all Other policy area.

source.section: Step 3 — Flag the filings worth a second look

function.summary: Marks a filing for follow-up when it names no specific bill, or when its policy area is the catch-all Other — both mean the issue text did not pin down what was being lobbied for. A filing missing either judgment is not guessed; the step stops and says which filing it was.

corner_cases.case: a filing names a specific bill and has a policy area other than `Other`
corner_cases.expected: the filing is kept and not flagged for follow-up

corner_cases.case: a filing names a specific bill but its policy area is `Other`
corner_cases.expected: the filing is flagged for follow-up
the step fails, naming the filing, rather than flagging it either way

compiler_notes: The document says this is a reading aid, not a verdict — no score, ranking or recommendation column is rendered. The follow-up cell restates the two conditions Step 3 decided on and adds nothing.
A filing flagged for follow-up that matches neither condition stops the step: the flag and the data it was decided from would disagree, and the page must not show a flag it cannot account for.

The report's markup and stylesheet are the committed file app/seeds/data/tutorial_triage_report.html; TEMPLATE_PATH is bound to it when the tutorial project is seeded, the way the input CSV's path is. A missing file or a missing section stops the step rather than publishing a half-rendered page.
specific_issues is rendered inside a collapsed disclosure rather than a column of its own, so the reader can check the vagueness claim against the text without the table becoming unscannable.
This stage writes the HTML to disk and returns a file-path pointer rather than embedding the markup inline, which is practical at scale.

function.summary: Fills the committed report template — one row per surviving filing, in the order they arrived — with the reported spend, the primary ask, the issue text as filed, and, for a flagged filing, which of the previous step's two conditions flagged it.

corner_cases.case: a filing is not flagged for follow-up
corner_cases.expected: its follow-up cell is a dash — no reason is invented for it

corner_cases.case: a filing is flagged, names no bill, and sits in the catch-all Other area
corner_cases.expected: both reasons are listed, not just the first

corner_cases.case: the template file is missing, or has lost one of its sections
corner_cases.expected: the step fails, naming the file, rather than writing a partial page
